schema.description: A PERSON'S DECISION, AND THE ONLY PART OF THE SPEC ANYONE BUT THIS SERVICE MAY WRITE. It lives in the spec, not the status, because the portal writes through snowplow's /call, which builds only the main-resource path and so cannot reach the status subresource — the same reason the incident page records spec.lifecycle on a TroubleshootingReport. The portal merge-patches this object with the user's own token; nightly-review copies it onto status (phase, decidedBy, decidedAt, reason) on its next run, and a reader should take this field over status.phase until then. The chart's admission policies (templates/decision-policy.yaml in the nightly-review chart) keep every other spec field immutable to people, stamp decidedBy and decidedAt from the request itself so a client cannot say who decided, and allow exactly one change of mind: PrOpen to Rejected.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: a PrOpen decision names the BuilderPublish claim that opened the change request

phase.description: The two outcomes a person reaches from the portal. Merged is absent on purpose: a merge happens in the repository, and a reconciler reading the pull request back is what should record it, not a button.

reason.description: Why, in the decider's words. Optional; a rejection with a reason is what the next prompt change learns from.

decidedBy.description: STAMPED BY ADMISSION FROM request.userInfo.username; whatever the client sends is overwritten. For a portal user this is the identity in their authn-issued clientconfig, because snowplow's /call dials the apiserver as the caller.

decidedAt.description: STAMPED BY ADMISSION, from the apiserver's own clock as recorded in managedFields for this write — CEL has no now(). Whatever the client sends is overwritten.

claim.description: The BuilderPublish claim the portal created to open the change request. Required with PrOpen. Mirrored onto the review.krateo.io/publish-claim label, where the service records the claims it creates itself, so one selector finds both.
